| **1361-1362** | Additional outbreak following the Second Pandemic |
| **1460s** | Significant plague wave in Central Germany including Saxony-Anhalt |
| **1591** | Major plague epidemic (approximately 20% of population died) |
| **1660s** | Continuing plague activity in the region |
| **1682** | Documented severe plague outbreak in Halle (approximately 4,400 deaths out of ~10,000 population) |
| **1712 & 1730** | Additional recorded outbreaks in the early 18th century |

If counting smaller waves and regional variations within the broader area, some scholars estimate **up to a dozen plague incidents** affected Halle during these four centuries (1348-1770). The city remained in the path of recurrent plague cycles until modern sanitation measures eventually brought them under control in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

## Answer

Based on my research, **Matthias Grünewald**, the German Renaissance painter who created one of the most famous artistic depictions of *The Crucifixion* (specifically his work for the Isenheim Altarpiece, completed circa 1512-1516), died in **Halle (Saale)**, Germany, in August 1528.

### Plague Outbreaks in Halle (Saale)

Throughout the medieval and early modern periods, Halle experienced numerous documented plague epidemics. Based on historical records, there were **at least 7-8 major plague outbreaks** in Halle between the 14th and 18th centuries:

| Year | Event |
|------|-------|
| **1348** | Black Death arrived in Northern Germany, reaching the Halle region |
| **1356-1366** | Pestis Secunda (Second Plague Pandemic) affected the area |
| **1361-1362** | Additional outbreak following the Second Pandemic |
| **1460s** | Significant plague wave in Central Germany including Saxony-Anhalt |
| **1591** | Major plague epidemic (approximately 20% of population died) |
| **1660s** | Continuing plague activity in the region |
| **1682** | Documented severe plague outbreak in Halle (approximately 4,400 deaths out of ~10,000 population) |
| **1712 & 1730** | Additional recorded outbreaks in the early 18th century |

If counting smaller waves and regional variations within the broader area, some scholars estimate **up to a dozen plague incidents** affected Halle during these four centuries (1348-1770). The city remained in the path of recurrent plague cycles until modern sanitation measures eventually brought them under control in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
